distinction: Wide open outdoor scenes with hazy distant landscape (mountains, valleys, grass fields) versus close-up furry animals and round or radial objects.
positive: Open landscapes with distant hills, sky and grassy fields; also a ball on grass and some bright smooth indoor objects. Heat spreads over whole scene.
negative: Close-up furry dogs and small animals, a daisy, radial wheel shapes, a tall tower; subject fills the frame.

distinction: Fires on the head and face of white-and-brown or tan floppy-eared spaniel-type dogs; negative for white fluffy wolf or husky types and for arches and buses.
positive: Heads of long-eared, brown-and-white or reddish smooth-coated dogs (spaniel, setter, hound); also a duck head. Heat sits on the muzzle and face.
negative: White or grey pointy-eared wolf and husky dogs, fluffy white dogs, stone arches, vehicles, towers.

distinction: Small perched songbirds with a red, orange or yellow breast on branches; negative for big dogs and round or radial objects.
positive: Small birds (finch, robin, junco, chickadee) perched on twigs, with warm orange or red chest; heat on the body.
negative: Large dogs (shepherd, hound, St Bernard), a car wheel, a dome, a bikini; shaggy lying dogs.

distinction: Small head or face-like detail of dog or animal lying in lap or small handheld gadgets; negative for round dial or clock and radial-pattern things.
positive: Mixed: dog faces lying down, phone in hand, harmonica and sax near a mouth, small grilles and keypad-like grids. Heat small and local on a face or keypad.
negative: Round dials and clocks, umbrellas and radial pinwheels, domes, pot-like round things.

distinction: Fires on covered or clothed human body parts and head coverings (caps, helmets, swimwear, scarves, doll clothes) versus wheeled vehicles and domes.
positive: Worn garments and head coverings on people or dolls: hats, helmets, bikinis, skirts, black head scarves; heat on the clothing area (waist, legs, helmet).
negative: Wheeled vehicles (bikes, mopeds, rickshaws, carts, cab), domes, fluffy shaggy dogs, boxy furniture.

distinction: Fires on criss-cross wire mesh or fence grids and net-like lattices, even faint, over the whole frame; negative for smooth round or glassy single objects.
positive: Chain-link fences, wire cages and nets in front of a subject; also lattices such as netting and volleyball nets. Heat spreads over the mesh.
negative: Smooth round or shiny single objects: wheel, sink, clock, jugs, slow cooker, rifle, beaker.

distinction: Fires on interlocking linked or woven metal-like texture (chains, chain mail) and small furry animals on branches; negative for smooth plain round objects.
positive: Chain links, chain mail, mesh, fence wire; also small animals (monkeys, spider, penguins) with busy rough texture. Heat covers the textured region.
negative: Smooth, plain, rounded objects: digital clocks, buckets, balloon, soccer ball, church, bottle, pug in clothes.

distinction: Small compact glossy object sitting alone on a plain or rough ground, such as a green beetle, dumbbell or bottle; negative for dogs lying down at close range.
positive: Small isolated shiny item centred on a plain background: green beetles, dumbbells, bottle cap, screwdriver, small bird on branch; also green vegetables. Heat is a small spot.
negative: Brown-and-white or tan dogs lying or sitting, hamsters, small pets in soft indoor settings.

distinction: Fires on the legs and lower body of a standing medium or large dog on the ground, seen whole from a distance; negative for close-up faces and for shiny household objects.
positive: Full-body standing dogs and similar four-legged animals (hare, wallaby, hyena, horse cart) on grass or pavement; heat sits on the legs and paws near the ground.
negative: Close-up dog faces, shiny metal or glass household objects (shakers, bottles, cup, lamp, wheel), tents, ambulance.

distinction: Fires on pale glowing or soft plumes against a dark or sky background (candle flame, fountains, geyser steam) and on white fluffy dogs; negative for dark glossy objects, dials and dark short-coated dogs.
positive: Bright soft plumes and flames: candle, fountain, geyser steam, smoke; tall red crane; very white curly or long-haired dogs. Heat on the plume or white shape.
negative: Glass of beer, dials and gauges, sunglasses, short-coated brown or spotted dogs, mushroom.

distinction: Fires on the head and face of light-coloured, golden, tan or red retriever-type dogs seen from the side; negative for domes, radial or fan shapes and fox-like dogs.
positive: Heads of golden, red-brown or white long-eared dogs (retriever, setter, hound) outdoors; heat is on the head.
negative: Domes and vaults, radial umbrella or fan shapes, goblets; pointed-ear fox-like or short-coated small dogs and foxes.

distinction: Fires on the head and chest of black-and-tan or black-white-brown dogs with three-colour patches; negative for pale or white animals and tall odd objects.
positive: Black dogs with tan and white markings (Rottweiler, Doberman, Bernese, Greater Swiss types); heat on head and chest. Weaker on dark small animals.
negative: Pale or white dog, parachute, airliner, microphone, hen, monkey on branch, baby, tractor.

distinction: Fires on bare or tight-clothed human torsos and tan-brown coats of animals at mid distance; negative for white plastic muzzles, dials, bees, spiders and boxy vehicles.
positive: People in swimwear or fitted clothes, volleyball players, tan or red-brown dog bodies and fur; heat low on the torso or body. Also flat green or plain colour patches.
negative: Muzzles over dog snouts, rotary phone, ladle, stopwatch, bee, spider, white vans, projector, mailbox.

distinction: Fires on a small round dial or rounded dark-and-light part, and on small perched birds or other single small subjects; negative for dogs lying facing the camera and for emergency vehicles.
positive: Round gauge or scale dials, spindles, small perched birds (bulbul, coot, chickadee) and monkeys; heat on one small round or rounded spot.
negative: Police van and ambulance, close-up tan and brown dogs (boxer, pekinese, retriever), fox, leopard.

distinction: Fires on seats and open-frame seating or carts for people (folding chairs, barber chairs, benches, rickshaws), often with a red or blue seat; negative for domes, radial patterns, and furry animal faces behind mesh.
positive: Chairs and seats: folding chair, swing seat, barber chair, rickshaw, bench, rocking chair; also cassette, scooter. Heat on the seat.
negative: Umbrella and dome radial patterns, vault, foxes, monkeys, cougar behind mesh, black widow spider, sunglasses.

distinction: Fires on the face of small slender furry mammals (ferret, weasel, cat, fox, hamster); negative for long-eared spaniel or large tri-colour dogs sitting.
positive: Faces and heads of small wild or cat-like furry animals: ferrets, weasels, tabby cats, foxes, hamsters. Heat on the face.
negative: Spaniels, Saint Bernard, mastiff and other large sitting dogs with long ears; also oil filter, ambulance, tile roof.

distinction: Fires on the body of a lone, thin-legged or perching wild bird against open ground, water or sky; negative for fluffy white or light dogs.
positive: Wild birds seen whole and small in the frame (water birds, finches, waders, storks, quail, partridge); heat on the bird body.
negative: Fluffy white, cream or light-coloured dogs close up, plus wall clock, dumbbell, CD player, mosque, old pickup.

distinction: Weak, broad firing on pale or white animals, especially dogs with open mouths, lit smooth skin or pale coat; negative for vehicles, bright coloured spokes, and green or spotted reptiles and beetles.
positive: White or cream dogs and arctic animals, mouths and tongues, lips, smooth skin tone patches; heat soft and spread around the face or mouth.
negative: Police van, cab, garbage truck, umbrella spokes, digital clock, green beetle and snake, daisy, shopping carts.

distinction: Fires on a hard, shiny, hanging or looped metal or string-like object (necklace, chain with padlock, lock, bolo tie, pan handle) and on bike or tractor wheels; negative for long-legged pale sighthounds and runners.
positive: Loops, chains, cords and shiny metal rims or handles: necklace, padlock, frying pan, basket, bike and tractor; heat on a ring or loop.
negative: Borzoi and other slender long-haired dogs, sailboat, apple on branch, snake, deerhound running, lab coats, computer, sandals.

distinction: Fires on a small bright bird, often yellow, on a branch, and other compact light creatures in a plain setting; negative for brown-and-white spaniels and cats.
positive: Small perched birds (goldfinch, chickadee, stork), a polar bear on ice, small pale pets; heat on the bird body.
negative: Red-and-white spaniels and cats lying down (springer, Blenheim, tabby, lynx), a lock, minibus.

distinction: Fires on the pointed snout and muzzle of slim or long-nosed dogs seen from the side; negative for screws, white storks and lying spaniels or cats facing the camera.
positive: Narrow muzzles and noses of long-nosed dogs (wolf, setter, collie, whippet, borzoi, husky); heat on the snout tip.
negative: Threaded screw, hound lying down, spaniel, stork, espresso cup, cat face, stage, desktop computer, reptiles.

distinction: Fires on plain man-made household items with flat or boxy shape and printed watermark text, over broad areas (safe, apron, mosquito net, mortar, carton); negative for gadgets with dials, keys or buttons.
positive: Plain household or shop objects in product photos (whistle, safes, apron, mortar, tube, mosquito nets, nails, projector); heat spread in horizontal bands, strongest on image watermark text.
negative: Scale with keypad, combination lock, phone, typewriter keys, cannon, solar panel, old tractor, reel, some shaggy dogs.

distinction: Fires on rising plumes or sprays of water or steam (fountains, geysers, fireboat jets) with soft vertical shape; negative for lone animals, pump or cup shapes on plain ground.
positive: Fountains, geysers, steam and water jets, lit sprays at night; also some furry monkeys in trees. Heat on the plume.
negative: Hyena, cats, gas pump, digital watch, dhole, eagle, mugs, beer glass, baboons.

distinction: Fires on hard machine parts with round dials, lenses, wheels or rivets (locomotives, watches, cameras, drums, cars); negative for human swimwear, round radial wheel hubs, clock faces and birds with long bills.
positive: Machinery and gadgets: trains, watch, camera lens, bottle caps, drum, tractor wheels, vintage cars. Heat on grilles, lenses, wheel or rivet detail.
negative: Swimsuits, turbine wheel hub, clock face, shorebirds with long bills, cougar eye, hoopskirt.

distinction: Fires on spotted or speckled coats and patterned bodies (dalmatian, leopard, hyena, spotted dogs); negative for plain-faced close-up shaggy dog faces and flowers.
positive: Spotted, dappled or blotched fur on the body of dogs and big cats; also dial faces with many small marks. Heat across the patterned flank.
negative: Close-up faces of shaggy or silky dogs, a daisy, golden retriever nose, duck, collie, leopard head, jay.

distinction: Weak firing on small light or mixed-colour dogs and animals sitting in grass or a lap, whole body in view; negative for reddish short-coated dogs, hounds and brown round nuts.
positive: Small or medium white, black-and-white or spotted dogs and birds sitting or standing in open setting; heat on the animal body.
negative: Red-brown smooth-coated dogs and spaniels, chestnuts and buckeyes, macaque, hamster, tiger face.

distinction: Fires on a pair of dark or glassy shapes set on a face or object (sunglasses, goggles, lenses, headlamp, bra cups), at the middle of the image; negative for long-legged wading birds and thin spidery shapes.
positive: Sunglasses, goggles, helmet visors, bra cups, headlights, round dark circles and bokeh; heat at the centre of a paired dark pattern.
negative: Wading shorebirds and geese, bulbul on branch, cyclist, harvestman spider, screws, stupa, computer.

distinction: Fires on dogs and people seen small in an outdoor scene and on long arched bridges and viaducts; negative for smooth rounded jugs, pots and dispensers.
positive: Spaniel-type dogs at distance with people, plus stone arch viaducts and bridges; heat on the dog body or the arched span.
negative: Smooth ceramic or glass vessels: teapots, soap dispensers, jugs, perfume bottle, pot; also tennis ball, scarf, mower.

distinction: Fires on small buttoned control gadgets and on dotted or spotted skin and fur (remote controls, dalmatian, hyena, leopard); negative for round clock faces, domes and plain cat or drink shapes.
positive: Grids of small buttons (remote controls, keypads, cassette player) and spotted coats of dogs and wild cats; heat on spots or buttons.
negative: Round clock and compass faces, church, umbrella spokes, Siamese cat, glass of drink, red car.

distinction: Broad firing on a thin vertical or slender object or limb held in a busy scene (swab, horn, sax, stick-like parts, striped zebras, spotty animals, wire rack); negative for large cat-like or bird-of-prey faces and glowing round objects.
positive: Thin straight parts and criss-cross rack lines: cat in a dishwasher rack, horn, sax, swab, bike riders, zebras, crane; heat along thin vertical lines and stripes.
negative: Face close-ups of raptor, albatross, German shepherd, fox, lesser panda; lighthouse, matchsticks in a heart, pinwheel.

distinction: Very faint firing on small bright-coloured creatures or objects against a muted background, such as small birds, flies and ladybugs; very weak, wide-spread and unclear.
positive: Small colourful birds and insects perched on twigs or ground (indigo bunting, bee eater, redshank, fly, ladybug); heat on the body. Also fine bright patterned textures.
negative: Almost nothing strong: dogs with shaggy faces, keyboards, bottles, cassette player, digital watch, pyjama shorts.

distinction: Fires on the head and bill of large long-necked or big-billed birds (ostrich, albatross, hornbill, crane); negative for round pots, jars and cups of drink.
positive: Heads and beaks of large birds: ostrich, hornbill, albatross, crane, goose, swan, toucan; heat on the head and bill.
negative: Round slow cooker, pots, saltshaker, church, glass drinks, jug, candle, car, gong.

distinction: Fires on the head of black, white and tan three-colour dogs (Swiss mountain types) and on green broccoli florets; negative for plain tan or fawn short-coated dogs.
positive: Heads and chests of black, white and tan dogs (Bernese, Swiss mountain, spaniels); green broccoli and leafy greens. Heat on the dog head.
negative: Tan or fawn short-haired large dogs (bloodhound, Great Dane, mastiff, Ridgeback, Ibizan), power drill, goose.

distinction: Weak, diffuse firing on a dark rounded or armoured object shown against a plain scene and on people in costume or swimwear; negative for round clocks and compasses, daisy and wheel.
positive: Mixed weak: Dutch oven pot, hatchet, armoured or uniformed people, bearskin hat, swimsuit, hare ears, small fluffy dogs; heat broad and low.
negative: Round dial faces: clocks, compasses, barometers; also car wheel hub, daisy, jars and washbasin.
